High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Jabalpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
This is fifth bail application of applicant Gopal Ahirwar and second bail application of applicant Brijlal Ahirwar filed under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of regular bail relating to FIR No.161/2023 dated 02.03.2023 registered at Police Station Cantonment, District Sagar (M.P.) for commission of offence under Sections 363, 366A, 376(2)(n), 376(3), 370, 372, 373,
34 of IPC and Section 5L/6 of the POCSO Act, 2012.
Applicant Gopal Ahirwar is in detention since 19.03.2023 and applicant Brijlal Ahirwar is in detention since 21.03.2023.
2. Applicant-Brijlal's first bail application was dismissed for want of prosecution vide order dated 21.09.2023 passed in M.Cr.C.No.14962 of 2023.
Applicant-Gopal Ahirwar's first bail application was dismissed for want of prosecution vide order dated 21.06.2023 passed in M.Cr.C.No.17623 of 2023.

Second, third and fourth bail applications of Gopal were dismissed as withdrawn and not pressed vide order dated 19.07.2023 passed in M.Cr.C.No.27490/2023, order dated 31.08.2023 passed in M.Cr.C.No.38708/2023 and order dated 20.10.2023 passed in M.Cr.C.No.46339/2023.
3.
As per the prosecution story, on 02.03.2023, prosecutrix mother lodged FIR about missing of her 14 years old daughter.
FIR was registered for commission of offence under Section 363 of IPC.
On 18.03.2023, she was recovered from village Gugwara District Chhatarpur.

In her statement under Section 161 and 164 of Cr.P.C. minor prosecutrix informed that Rajesh Jatav had kidnapped her and thereafter he along with his maternal uncle Gopal Ahirwar sold her to Brijlal Ahirwar for a consideration of Rs.40,000/-.
After purchasing her, Brijlal repeatedly committed rape/aggravated penetrative sexual assault upon her.
After investigation, charge sheet has been filed for commission of aforesaid offences.
4. Learned counsel for the applicants have submitted that applicants have not committed any offence.
They are innocent.
They have been falsely implicated.
Learned counsel for applicant Brijlal has argued that prosecutrix has already been examined before the trial Court.
Now there is no possibility of influencing or tempering with the prosecution evidence.
It is further submitted that only allegation against him is of purchasing a minor girl for a consideration of Rs.40,000/-.
It is submitted that he was informed that prosecutrix is a major.

Learned counsel has referred some questions and answers of the cross- examination of the minor prosecutrix and has submitted that in her cross- examination she had admitted that Brijlal had consensually established sexual relations with her.
Therefore, it is prayed that applicant Brijlal may be released on bail.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for applicant-Gopal has also referred to examination- in-chief and cross-examination of the prosecutrix and has submitted that Gopal was neither involved in human trafficking nor he had any role in sale of the prosecutrix by accused Rajesh.
He has been implicated only because he is the relative of Rajesh.
Therefore, it is prayed that applicant Gopal may be released on bail.
6. On the other hand, learned Panel Lawyer for the State has opposed grant of bail and has submitted that it is a case of human trafficking of minor girl.
She was sold, purchased and consumed like an article, such act of accused person have shocked the conscience of the society.
If bail is granted in such matters, same will give wrong signal to the society.
However, learned counsel for the complainant has submitted that he has no objection if Gopal Ahirwar is released on bail.
7. Learned counsel for applicant Brijlal has submitted that affidavit has been filed in which NOC has been given to Brijlal also for grant of bail.
8. I have gone through the material on record.
It is a case where a minor girl aged 14 years was taken away from her home by one Rajesh and thereafter he along with Gopal sold her for a consideration of Rs.40,000/-.
Purchaser of the girl repeatedly committed rape/aggravated penetrative sexual assault upon her.
It is noteworthy that sale of girl was documented on stamp paper.
Having taken into consideration all the facts and circumstances of the case including gravity of offence, I am of the view that it is not a fit case for grant of bail.

9. As far as the evidence of prosecutrix before the trial Court is concerned, as per the law laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Satish Jaggi Vs. State of Chhattisgarh and others (2007) 11 SCC 195 High Court is not required to appreciate the evidence which has been recorded during trial as it has to see prima-facie case only at the time of deciding bail.

sentences.text: 10. Therefore, for the aforementioned reasons, this fifth bail application filed on behalf of applicant-Gopal Ahirwar and second bail application filed on behalf of applicant-Brijlal Ahirwar, are dismissed.
